excerpts.raw:
Journal de la SNHF (1827-1910)
1828: ya tienes precios en mercado hablan de su cultivo y de ensayos de injertos sobre patata
1830: conserva en salmuera

1834: Nombran tomate hâtive. Tomate precoz

1835: hablan de introduccion de variedades de otros cultivos y que transportaban el tomate desde el Midi a Paris

1839: Vilmorin expone el tomate cereza. M. Boisse tomate grosse

1840: Gallois tomate hâtive
1841; Vilmorin: tomate cerise, poire y gross jaune
1843: mortermat trae de Italia tomate poire pequeño, pero dice que ya lo tenia vilmorin y otros

1848: Masson: tomate gross jaune. Vilmorin tomate pire

1850: viaje a haiti, pequeño rojo palido.la compara con la rojo grande

1851: el consumo en UK viene de españa y del midi.
Masson uestra tomate gross jaune y cerise jaune
cide: tomate poire, cereza y rojo comun

1853: hablan de jaune grosse, jaune ronde, jaune cereise
de tomates enanos precoces
tomate mostruoso
1855: exposicion universal, se centran en exponer variedades de cultivo, pero no dicen cuales
Crude. 5 variedades nuevas de tomate, renovacion de variedades horticolas

1857 Crean una variedad que pertenece al tipo tomate de Naples, dicen que son grandes pero no estan buenos
1859: tomates de primeur presentados por Millet. Tomate grosse de Bayonne
1861: tomates hatives. Tomate poire de Naples. Tomates de Bayonne. Rouge grosse. una nueva variedad fijada por M.Ponce

1862: dicen que tomates peras de semillas traidas de Naples duran mas y que en Naples las dejan inclusio en el campo. variedades de tomate de adorno . Tomate rojo precoz. tomate rojo y amarillo

1863: tomates grandes que vienen de perpignan
1865: semillas de china de horticolas que son variedades europeas de vuelta
1868: una tomate de senegal pero dicen que es un tomate cereza
1869. grosse hative. Tomate groiselle (solanum racemigerum ==pimpi)
1870: tomates enormes importados de inglaterra.
1872. Tomate de forma regular redondo (remarcable). Uno piensa que es un hibrido con el tomate cereza, intermedio. Pero otro que es un nuevo tipo de tomate-
1873. Habla de Grosse tardive y de una posible nueva variedad. Tambien comentan el tomate pomme desarrollado en America. y que debe ser la que presento brudeuaux.
Otro amateur presenta tomate redondo liso: tomate brune de Charny
1874: Tomate Trophy
1875. Tomates pequeños de fantasia, sin utilidad. tomate naine native, tomate groiselle
1876, tomate naine. Rouge gross hative
1877. tomate grosse rouge lise saus cotes
1878: tomates sanos que se mantienen solo colgandolos al aire seco. traen de japon tomates pequeños muy precoces, pero que segun ellos son brune de charny. tomates cerices. hablan de 12, 8 variedades de tomate de cada productor pero no las nombran
1879. tomate-pimiento de egipto que lo usan como condimento, No se que es . em 1880 dicen que es awada, no tiene que ver nada
1880: tomate cerise

excerpts.translation:
Journal de la SNHF (1827-1910)
1828: you already have market prices, they speak of its cultivation and of grafting trials on potato
1830: preservation in brine

1834: They name early tomato. Early tomato

1835: they speak of introduction of varieties from other crops and that they transported the tomato from the Midi to Paris

1839: Vilmorin exhibits the cherry tomato. M. Boisse large tomato

1840: Gallois early tomato
1841; Vilmorin: cherry tomato, pear and large yellow
1843: mortermat brings from Italy small pear tomato, but says that Vilmorin and others already had it

1848: Masson: large yellow tomato. Vilmorin pear tomato

1850: trip to Haiti, small pale red. He compares it with the large red

1851: consumption in the UK comes from Spain and from the Midi.
Masson shows large yellow tomato and yellow cherry
cide: pear tomato, cherry and common red

1853: they speak of large yellow, round yellow, cherry yellow
of early dwarf tomatoes
monstrous tomato
1855: Universal Exhibition, they focus on exhibiting cultivation varieties, but do not say which ones
Crude. 5 new varieties of tomato, renewal of horticultural varieties

1857 They create a variety that belongs to the Naples tomato type, they say they are large but not good
1859: early tomatoes presented by Millet. Large tomato from Bayonne
1861: early tomatoes. Pear tomato from Naples. Tomatoes from Bayonne. Large red. A new variety fixed by M. Ponce

1862: they say that pear tomatoes from seeds brought from Naples last longer and that in Naples they leave them even in the field. ornamental tomato varieties. Early red tomato. Red and yellow tomato

1863: large tomatoes that come from Perpignan
1865: seeds from China of horticulturalists that are European varieties returned
1868: a tomato from Senegal but they say it is a cherry tomato
1869. large early. Gooseberry tomato (solanum racemigerum == pimpi)
1870: enormous tomatoes imported from England.
1872. Tomato of regular round shape (remarkable). One thinks it is a hybrid with the cherry tomato, intermediate. But another that is a new type of tomato-
1873. Speaks of large late and of a possible new variety. They also comment on the apple tomato developed in America. and that it must be the one presented by Brudeaux.
Another amateur presents smooth round tomato: brown tomato from Charny
1874: Trophy Tomato
1875. Small fantasy tomatoes, without utility. native dwarf tomato, gooseberry tomato
1876, dwarf tomato. Large early red
1877. large smooth red tomato without ribs
1878: healthy tomatoes that are kept only by hanging them in dry air. They bring from Japan very early small tomatoes, but according to them they are brown from Charny. Cherry tomatoes. They speak of 12, 8 varieties of tomato from each producer but do not name them
1879. eggplant-tomato from Egypt that they use as a condiment, I don't know what it is. in 1880 they say it is awada, it has nothing to do with it
1880: cherry tomato
